title: Stage Gate Guardian for SLO-driven Model Ejections
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: We currently rely on static, single-metric thresholds to abort model rollouts. That leads to brittle (false positive) ejections during traffic spikes and misses gradual degradations in token cost or percentile latency. Goal: Ship an adaptive stage-gate service that computes a composite health score across configured SLOs (p99 latency, 95th token cost, error-rate, and throughput delta), applies cohort-aware burn-in and hysteresis, and triggers deterministic ejections ('ejections' = automatic removal of a candidate model from live traffic) while preserving operator visibility and manual override. This ticket implements the core signal fusion, decision engine, and telemetry hooks needed by canary/A-B/shadow workflows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New 'stage-gate' microservice receives telemetry from canaries and shadow runs and emits deterministic ejection decisions and a human-readable reason code.
2) Composite health score computed from at least four signals: latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate, token-cost-per-response, and throughput; weights are configurable per-project.
3) Burn-in window (configurable default 5 minutes) prevents premature ejection; hysteresis prevents thrash via ramp-down/backoff rules.
4) Bayesian sequential test with configurable alpha/beta reduces false positives for low-volume cohorts.
5) Operator UI in Console shows score timeline, contributing signal breakdown, and an immediate 'hold' override button.
6) End-to-end integration tests and synthetic traffic scenarios demonstrate >95% precision/recall on labeled failure simulations.
7) Docs, runbook, and a PR with unit/integration tests merged to main and can be toggled on/off with a feature flag.
implementation_notes:
Design highlights:
- Composite score: normalized z-scores per metric -> weighted sum -> logistic transform to [0,1] where lower values indicate healthier.
- Token-cost delta treated as per-request marginal cost normalized by baseline (cost SLO triggers when moving average exceeds threshold and derivative is positive).
- Bayesian sequential test: use Beta-Binomial for error-rate and Gaussian conjugate for latency percentiles; compute posterior probability that candidate is worse than baseline by delta. Trigger only if posterior > configurable threshold (default 0.95) and traffic volume > minimum samples.
- Cohorts: traffic is partitioned by customer-tier, region, and client-version; decision engine evaluates cohorts independently and can apply weighted global ejection when multiple cohorts exceed thresholds.
- Burn-in & hysteresis: initial grace period (T_burnin) where only 'soft' alerts are emitted; a second window for re-evaluation prevents oscillation. Use exponential backoff for re-introductions.
- Shadow/seed mode: allow routing of mirrored traffic to candidate without impacting production, use it to prime priors for Bayesian tests.
- Telemetry: add per-decision trace id, contributing metric deltas, posterior probabilities, and cohort tags.
- Safety: automatic ejection must publish a deterministic event to Kafka and create a console incident with suggested revert plan.
- Operator controls: allow manual immediate eject, hold, or force-pass with audit trail.
Implementation tasks: core service (Go), scoring library (Rust -> Wasm), telemetry adapters (Python ingestion hooks), console UI changes (React).
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag and enable in staging only.
2) Week 1: Enable shadow mode for 10% of traffic for high-volume models; collect priors and verify telemetry.
3) Week 2: Enable soft alerts (no auto-eject) for 25% of canaries; validate composite score and dashboarding.
4) Week 3: Enable auto-eject for internal projects with conservative thresholds (posterior>0.995, min samples=200).
5) Week 4: Gradually relax thresholds to default and expand to customer-facing canaries.
6) Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window, weekly pass/fail review meetings, and a contingency plan to rollback feature flag.
Operational knobs: ejection scope (cohort-only vs global), sensitivity (posterior threshold), minimum-sample gates, and token-cost weight.
Fallback: if the service fails, auto-eject is disabled and only alerts are emitted; traffic continues to baseline model.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring math, z-score normalization, and logistic transform.
- Simulated traffic harness: replay production traces with injected latency/error/cost regressions to validate decision timing and false-positive rates.
- Shadow run acceptance: seed Bayesian priors with mirrored requests and assert posterior confidence converges before any auto-eject enabled.
- Chaos test: randomly delay telemetry to verify burn-in/hysteresis prevents premature ejection when signals are delayed.
- Load test: ensure stage-gate service sustains decision throughput for 5k decisions/sec with <50ms median decision latency.
- Integration test: end-to-end with Console UI, Kafka events, and incident automation.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Overly-sensitive thresholds could cause unnecessary ejections and customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults, Bayesian tests, and mandatory minimum-sample gates.
Risk: Telemetry delays create false positives. Mitigation: implement delay-aware burn-in and soft-alert mode.
Risk: Complexity increases on-call burden. Mitigation: automated explainability (reason codes), runbook, and automated rollback only when multiple independent signals align.
Risk: Cost SLO miscalibration could bias ejections toward cheaper but lower-quality variants. Mitigation: normalize cost signal and bound its weight relative to latency/error signals.
